page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, set right of centre, with no marginal notes. A handwritten mark sits at top left and is left out. The right edge of the scan cuts into the last letters of some lines. Running head at top, page number 430 with it. Text ends with a catchword at bottom right.

municipale, seu statutum, vulgo Wilkhür / Weic-
Quis autem possit condere statuta, dicit Schneide-
vvinus ad §.jus autem civil.inst.hoc titulo.

l.i: Quid est Jus Civile privatum non scriptum?

main_text.l: Est quod usus approbavit. Nam diuturni mores,
consensu utentium comprobati, legem imitantur. §.
sine scripto, inst. cod. Et dicitur Consuetudo Spec-
ialis. Quomodo autem consuetudo introducatur,
docet Schneidevvinus hic.
Naturalia quidem jura, quæ apud omnes gentes
peræque observantur. Divina quadam providentia
constituta, semper firma atque immutabilia perma-
nent. Ea vero quæ ipsa sibi quæque civitas constituit
sæpe mutari solent, vel tacito consensu populi, vel
alia postea lege lata.§.sed natural.inst.eod.
Omne jus, quo utimur, vel ad personas pertinet,
(quibus jus redditur) vel ad res (de quibus jus reddi-
tur) vel ad actiones (per quas jus redditur.) Et prius
de personis videamus. Nam parum est jus nosse, si
personæ, quarum causa constitutum est, ignorentur.
§.final.inst.eod. Vide Vvesenbecium[?] super institut.
QUIS EST TERTIUS
De Jure Personarum. Vom Recht
Summa divisio personarum hæc est, quod omnes

page.notes: Right edge of the scan cuts off the last letters of several lines (e.g. "constituit", "consensu", "introducatur"); those words are read from the visible parts. "Vvesenbecium" is doubtful: the second letter could be "e" or "c". The black-letter words "Wilkhür", "Weichbild/oder Stattrecht", "Vom Recht" and "der Personen." are read from the scan and may be imperfect. The title "QUIS EST TERTIUS" is an ordinal without a Roman numeral, so no caput number is given. The handwritten mark at top left is omitted.
